exposure: Model of care (public insurance, chosen doctor in public system, chosen midwife in public system, private midwife-led community birth)
cohort: The study included 1257 Hungarian women who completed an online survey regarding their birth experiences across four different models of care.
finding: Hungarian women who planned community births had significantly lower rates of obstetric procedures and disrespectful care, alongside higher levels of autonomy, compared to those in public hospital care models.
mod_finding: Planning community births was associated with significantly reduced odds of cesarean, induced labor, and episiotomy.
